# LNT v5

> LNT is LLVM's performance-monitoring server. Build bots submit benchmark
> results to it; it stores them as time series and serves them back so that
> performance changes can be found, investigated and tracked. Everything it
> holds is available through the REST API described below.

## Documentation

- [OpenAPI specification](/api/openapi.json): every parameter, request body,
  response body and status code. Consult it for anything this file leaves out.
- [Interactive documentation](/api/docs): the same specification, for humans.
- [API index](/api): links to the suite list endpoint and to both of the above.

## Concepts

- **Test suite** -- a namespace with a schema of its own. Nearly every endpoint
  lives under `/api/suites/{testsuite}/`, and nothing is shared between suites:
  two suites may hold machines of the same name and they are different machines.
  `GET /api/suites` returns every suite with its schema.
- **Schema** -- a suite declares its `metrics`, `machine_fields` and
  `commit_fields` up front. Each entry has a `name` and a `type`: `real`,
  `integer`, `text` or `datetime`. Nothing undeclared can be stored: a metric or
  a field the schema does not name is rejected with 400 rather than ignored.
- **Machine** -- where a benchmark ran, addressed by `name`. Carries the
  declared `machine_fields` under `fields`, and a built-in `tracked` flag
  marking whether it takes part in *automatic* machine selection, such as a
  dashboard picking which machines to show.
- **Commit** -- what was benchmarked, addressed by an identity string `value`
  (a Git SHA, a version, or an ad-hoc label like `experiment-vectorizer-v2`).
  Carries the declared `commit_fields` under `fields`, plus two optional
  built-ins: `ordinal`, an integer placing the commit in the suite's total order,
  and `tag`, a label such as `release-18.1`. An ordinal is never inferred, not
  even from a numeric commit string. A commit without one has no position, so it
  is absent from every result ordered by ordinal. Listing commits orders them
  by when the server first saw each one by default (`sort=first_seen`), keeping
  every commit; `sort=-first_seen` puts the most recently seen first.
  `after_commit=` and `before_commit=` bound the list by ordinal.
- **Run** -- one submission of results for one machine at one commit,
  identified by a UUID. Several runs may share a machine and a commit.
- **Test** -- a benchmark name, created implicitly by submission. Test names
  contain `/`, so no path ever carries one: a test is named in a `test=` query
  parameter or in a request body. Machine names and commit values do appear in
  paths, so they may not contain `/` or be `.` or `..`.
- **Sample** -- one measurement of one test in one run: `{test, metrics}`, where
  `metrics` holds only the metrics that have a value. A test measured several
  times in one run yields one sample per repetition.
- **Profile** -- optional instruction-level counter data for one test in one
  run. It is submitted inline with the run, as a test entry's `profile`: a JSON
  document, gzip-compressed and base64-encoded. It is read back through its own
  UUID, piecemeal or as that same document in plain JSON.
- **Regression** -- a performance change someone is tracking: a state, and
  optionally a title, a `bug` URL in an external tracker, a suspected commit and
  free-form notes, plus *indicators*, each naming one `(machine, test, metric)`
  the change was observed on. LNT does no detection of its own; an external
  analyzer reads the time series and records what it finds here.

## Endpoints

Every operation, with the scope it requires (see Authentication).

```
GET    /api                                                   read    API index
GET    /api/auth                                              read    The API key the request authenticated with
GET    /api/suites                                            read    Every suite, with its schema
POST   /api/suites                                            manage  Create a suite from a schema
GET    /api/suites/{name}                                     read    One suite's schema
PATCH  /api/suites/{name}/schema                              manage  Add, update or remove metrics and fields
DELETE /api/suites/{name}                                     manage  Delete a suite and all its data

GET    /api/suites/{testsuite}/machines                       read    List machines (search=, tracked=, sort=)
POST   /api/suites/{testsuite}/machines                       manage  Create a machine
GET    /api/suites/{testsuite}/machines/{machine_name}        read    One machine
PATCH  /api/suites/{testsuite}/machines/{machine_name}        manage  Update or rename a machine
DELETE /api/suites/{testsuite}/machines/{machine_name}        manage  Delete a machine and its runs

GET    /api/suites/{testsuite}/commits                        read    List commits (search=, machine=, before_commit=, sort=, ...)
POST   /api/suites/{testsuite}/commits                        submit  Create a commit
POST   /api/suites/{testsuite}/commits/resolve                read    Look up many commits by value at once
GET    /api/suites/{testsuite}/commits/{value}                read    One commit, with its previous/next by ordinal
PATCH  /api/suites/{testsuite}/commits/{value}                manage  Set or clear its ordinal, tag or fields
DELETE /api/suites/{testsuite}/commits/{value}                manage  Delete a commit and its runs

GET    /api/suites/{testsuite}/runs                           read    List runs (machine=, commit=, search=, sort=, ...)
POST   /api/suites/{testsuite}/runs                           submit  Submit a run
GET    /api/suites/{testsuite}/runs/{uuid}                    read    One run
DELETE /api/suites/{testsuite}/runs/{uuid}                    manage  Delete a run
GET    /api/suites/{testsuite}/runs/{uuid}/samples            read    A run's samples (test=)
GET    /api/suites/{testsuite}/runs/{uuid}/profiles           read    A run's profiles, as {test, uuid}

GET    /api/suites/{testsuite}/tests                          read    List tests (search=, machine=, metric=)

POST   /api/suites/{testsuite}/query                          read    Time-series data points for one metric
GET    /api/suites/{testsuite}/trends                         read    Per-commit geomeans, per machine

GET    /api/suites/{testsuite}/profiles/{uuid}                read    A profile's top-level counters
GET    /api/suites/{testsuite}/profiles/{uuid}/functions      read    Its functions, with their counters
GET    /api/suites/{testsuite}/profiles/{uuid}/disassembly    read    One function's instructions (function=)
GET    /api/suites/{testsuite}/profiles/{uuid}/document       read    The whole profile, as the document a submission carries

GET    /api/suites/{testsuite}/regressions                    read    List regressions (state=, machine=, search=, sort=, ...)
POST   /api/suites/{testsuite}/regressions                    triage  Create a regression
GET    /api/suites/{testsuite}/regressions/{uuid}             read    One regression, with its indicators
PATCH  /api/suites/{testsuite}/regressions/{uuid}             triage  Update title, bug, notes, state or commit
DELETE /api/suites/{testsuite}/regressions/{uuid}             triage  Delete a regression
POST   /api/suites/{testsuite}/regressions/{uuid}/indicators  triage  Add indicators
DELETE /api/suites/{testsuite}/regressions/{uuid}/indicators  triage  Remove indicators, by UUID
POST   /api/suites/{testsuite}/regressions/indicators/query   read    Indicators across regressions (machine, test, metric, state, commit)

GET    /api/admin/api-keys                                    admin   List API keys
POST   /api/admin/api-keys                                    admin   Create an API key
DELETE /api/admin/api-keys/{prefix}                           admin   Revoke an API key
```

Deleting a suite, or removing entries from its schema, destroys data and needs
`?confirm=true`.

## Conventions

- **List endpoints return objects**: `{"items": [...]}`, plus
  `"cursor": {"next": ..., "previous": null}` on a cursor-paginated endpoint,
  or `"total": N` on an offset-paginated one, which takes `offset=`.
  `/machines` is the only offset-paginated endpoint. `limit` defaults to 25,
  at most 10000.
- **Cursors**: send `cursor.next` back unchanged -- as `cursor=`, or as the
  `cursor` key of a request body -- with the same filters and `sort`; only
  `limit` may change. Stop when it is null. Never parse or build one.
- **Sorting**: `sort=<name>`, prefixed with `-` for descending.
- **Query parameters**: give several values by repeating the parameter
  (`?state=active&state=detected`). A parameter the endpoint does not take is
  400 rather than ignored, and so is repeating one that takes a single value.
- **Errors**: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`. Branch on `code`,
  never on `message`. The codes are `invalid_request` (400), `unauthorized`
  (401), `forbidden` (403), `not_found` (404), `method_not_allowed` (405, with
  an `Allow` header), `duplicate`, `conflict` and `retry` (409), and
  `internal_error` (500). A request body too large for the deployment is a
  plain-text 413 instead. Among the 409s:
  - `duplicate`: the entity exists. For a run or a regression whose UUID you
    chose, an earlier attempt most likely succeeded: do not resend under a fresh
    UUID, which would store it twice.
  - `conflict`: the request contradicts stored state -- metadata a submission
    disagrees with, an ordinal another commit holds, or a commit a regression
    still references. Do not retry as sent; change the request or the state
    first.
  - `retry`: a concurrent change to the suite's schema got in the way. Nothing
    was written; send the same request again.
- **Names that match nothing**: a run submission creates the machine, commit
  and tests it names. Everywhere else, an unknown machine or test is 404, an
  unknown metric or regression state is 400, and an unknown commit used as a
  filter (`commit=`, or the `commit` of `/query` or of the indicator lookup) is
  an empty result. A commit used as a range bound (`after_commit`,
  `before_commit`) is 404 if unknown and 400 if it has no ordinal. A commit a
  regression refers to is 404. A schema `PATCH` that updates or removes an
  entry the schema does not have is 404, metrics included.
- **Values**: timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC with a `Z` suffix. Values in
  `fields` and `metrics` use the JSON type their declared type calls for: a
  number for `real` and `integer`, never a string, so `"5"` is not accepted for
  an integer; a string for `text`; an ISO 8601 string for `datetime`.
- **References are flat**: a run carries `"machine": "linux-x86_64"` and
  `"commit": "abc123"`, not nested objects. `POST /commits/resolve` turns a page
  of commit values into full commits in one call.

## Authentication

Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Scopes form a hierarchy -- `read` <
`submit` < `triage` < `manage` < `admin` -- and a key grants its own scope and
every lower one. `read` endpoints allow anonymous access, so send no header if
you only read. A header that carries no usable Bearer token, or an unknown or
revoked one, is 401 even on a `read` endpoint, and too little scope is 403.
To check a token before relying on it, `GET /api/auth` returns the key it
belongs to, including the scope it grants.

## Workflows

Paths below are relative to `/api/suites/{testsuite}`. Metric and field names
in the examples are placeholders: use the ones the suite's schema declares.

**Submit a run** with `POST /runs`:

```json
{
  "format_version": "5",
  "machine": {"name": "linux-x86_64", "fields": {"os": "linux"}},
  "commit": {"value": "abc123", "ordinal": 593922, "fields": {"author": "Jane Doe"}},
  "run_parameters": {"build_config": "Release"},
  "tests": [
    {"name": "bench/foo", "execution_time": 1.23, "compile_time": 0.45},
    {"name": "bench/bar", "execution_time": [0.10, 0.11, 0.12], "compile_time": 0.40}
  ]
}
```

The machine and the commit are created if they do not exist. An array records
one sample per repetition. Every array in one test must have the same length,
and a scalar beside them is repeated in each of those samples: above,
`bench/bar` yields three samples, each with `compile_time` 0.40, so
aggregating per sample counts that value three times. `uuid` is optional and
generated when omitted. The submission is atomic, and answers 201 with the run.
It never overwrites what is stored: a field, tag or ordinal that differs from
the stored one is 409, and `PATCH` is the only way to change it. The machine's
`tracked` flag is the exception: it is set only when the submission creates the
machine, and ignored rather than compared afterwards.

**Chart a metric over time** with `POST /query`:

```json
{"metric": "execution_time", "machine": "linux-x86_64", "test": ["bench/foo"], "sort": "commit"}
```

Only `metric` is required. Other filters are `commit`, `after_commit`,
`before_commit`, `after_time` and `before_time`, and `sort` takes `test`,
`commit` (by ordinal) or `submitted_at`. Each point looks like:

```json
{"test": "bench/foo", "machine": "linux-x86_64", "metric": "execution_time",
 "value": 1.23, "commit": "abc123", "ordinal": 593922, "tag": null,
 "run_uuid": "573af861-8303-4a5b-a643-b8321e0142c4", "submitted_at": "2026-08-25T14:22:41Z"}
```

**Get an overview across machines** with
`GET /trends?metric=execution_time&machine=a&machine=b&last_n=100`. It returns
one `value` per (machine, commit), for the `last_n` most recent commits by
ordinal that have data. Each test's samples in a run are reduced by
`sample_agg` (`median` by default), the run's geomean is taken across tests, and
the runs at a commit are combined by another geomean. The metric must be
numeric.

**Follow up on a data point** through its `run_uuid`: `GET /runs/{uuid}`,
`GET /runs/{uuid}/samples?test=bench/foo`, and `GET /runs/{uuid}/profiles`. A
profile is then read through its own UUID; every counter is a raw count.
`GET /profiles/{uuid}/document` returns it whole: gzip-compressed and
base64-encoded.

**Compare a run with the previous commit on its machine**:
`GET /commits?machine=linux-x86_64&before_commit=abc123&sort=-ordinal&limit=1`
returns the nearest earlier commit at which that machine has runs, which the
commit's own `previous` may not be, and
`GET /runs?machine=linux-x86_64&commit={value}` lists those runs.

**Check what is already tracked** before recording a regression. A change is
tracked when a regression attributed to its commit has an indicator naming its
machine, test and metric. Check many at once with
`POST /regressions/indicators/query`:

```json
{"machine": ["linux-x86_64"], "test": ["bench/foo", "bench/bar"],
 "metric": "execution_time", "commit": "abc123"}
```

Every key is optional; `machine`, `test` and `state` are lists. It returns the
matching indicators across all regressions, each as `{uuid, regression_uuid,
machine, test, metric}`, cursor-paginated like `/query`: a (machine, test,
metric) it returns is already tracked at that commit. Read a regression itself
with `GET /regressions/{uuid}`.

**Record a regression** with `POST /regressions`:

```json
{"title": "foo slowdown", "commit": "abc123",
 "indicators": [{"machine": "linux-x86_64", "test": "bench/foo", "metric": "execution_time"}]}
```

Every key is optional; `bug`, `notes` and `state` are accepted too. The state
defaults to `detected`, and moves freely between `detected`, `active`,
`not_to_be_fixed`, `fixed` and `false_positive` through `PATCH`. As for a run,
`uuid` is optional and generated when omitted; choose your own to make the
request safe to retry.
